data.name: Faizee
data.gender_notes: Faizee is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who assists, supports, and aids in carrying out a task. The name Faizee carries the meaning “Helper” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Faizee usually hope their child will grow to embody helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: To serve and help others in the path of righteousness.
data.etymology: Faizee belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Faizee total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم فيزي مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ف-ض-ل' الذي يعني الزيادة والنمو في الخير والفضل. يرتبط هذا الاسم بمعاني الإكثار من الخيرات والبركات. استخدم هذا الاسم في الثقافة الإسلامية كدلالة على الشخص الذي يتميز بالكرم والسخاء.

in_urdu.name: فیزی
in_urdu.meaning: فضل سے ماخوذ، عظمت و رفعت کا مطلب
in_urdu.long_meaning: فیزی نام عربی جڑ 'ف-ض-ل' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے فضل، عظمت، اور رفعت. یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں اس شخص کی خصوصیت کے طور پر استعمال کیا جاتا ہے جو كرم، سخاء، اور عظیم اخلاق کا حامل ہے.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Faizee" is a name of Arabic origin, frequently found among the Ismaili and Shia communities within the Islamic faith. This name signifies the importance of community, unity, and cooperation in assisting one another in everyday life, particularly during times of need. It is a reminder of the collective responsibility of individuals within the community to support and uplift one another, as outlined in various Islamic teachings, such as the Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) "None of you will believe until you love for your brothers what you love for yourself" (Al Imam Ali (AS), Nahjul Balagha).
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Faizee" carries deeper meaning in relation to the service of God (Allah SWT) and the concept of assisting fellow believers. It is a reminder that each individual has a role to play in God's grand scheme, and that one way to serve God is by serving others. By embracing the name "Faizee," one can reflect on the divine values of compassion, kindness, and selflessness, as well as the importance of staying steadfast in one's faith and seeking God's guidance in all endeavors. Ultimately, the name "Faizee" serves as a constant invitation to deepen one's connection with God and to extend kindness and support to all of Creation, recognizing that all actions have spiritual consequences.

historical_references.reference: The Mughal Emperor Faizabad I (1556-1605 AD) was known as Faizee-ud-din. He ascended the throne at the age of thirty and ruled for over fifty years. Faizee was an able administrator and a just ruler. He expanded the Mughal Empire by conquering Malwa and Gujarat, bringing them under the Mughal rule for the first time.

The Islamic scholar Abul Hasan Al-Faizee (died around 1136 AD) was a leading theologian of the Ash'ari school of thought in Islam. He wrote extensively on various aspects of Islamic theology, including the nature of God, the attributes of Allah, the question of predestination, and the concept of prophethood. His most famous work is 'Kitab Al-Mabhut' (The Existent), which is a comprehensive summary of Ash'ari theology and has been a standard reference for scholars in this field for centuries.
